memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the account of the family of Aaron and Moses at the time the Lord spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai. The names of the sons of Aaron were Nadab the firstborn and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Those were the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests. - Num 3:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter opens by naming Aaron's sons — the anointed priests who were set apart to serve God. These men were given a high and holy privilege: to stand before God on behalf of the people. They were anointed and ordained for sacred work.

It is a reminder that God calls people by name into His service. Aaron's family was chosen not because they were flawless, but because God graciously appointed them. Their calling was a gift, not a reward they had earned.

We may not be Old Testament priests, but every believer in Christ has been given a priestly calling too. The New Testament says we are "a royal priesthood" (1 Pet 2:9), set apart to worship God and to represent Him to the world. That is an astonishing privilege.

Yet privilege always comes with responsibility. To be near to God is a gift; it is also a call to live worthy of that nearness. As we will soon see in this chapter, not all of Aaron's sons treated their calling with the reverence it deserved.

Today, remember the privilege you have been given in Christ — access to God, a calling to serve Him. Receive it with gratitude, and carry it with reverence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see your relationship with God as a privilege?
- What does it mean to live as one "set apart" for Him?
- How can you serve God faithfully today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the privilege of knowing You and serving You. Help me to treat this calling with gratitude and reverence. Amen.
